NORTHSTAR ELECTRONICS CONTROLLED QUALITY DOCUMENT
QSP-PCB-017 | Revision 1.0 | Portfolio demonstration Page 1
PCB Camera Inspection
Acceptance Specification
Example requirements for detector findings, deterministic disposition, and human review
Document QSP-PCB-017 Revision 1.0
Owner Quality Engineering Effective 13 September 2026
Applies to PCB optical inspection cell Status Example / not production
1. Purpose and decision authority
This example defines image-level acceptance logic for a PCB optical inspection cell. The detector supplies candidate regions
and confidence scores. The approved deterministic policy supplies the final PASS, FAIL, or HUMAN REVIEW disposition.
1.1. Approval gate
Rules extracted from this document are draft candidates only. A quality engineer must verify the cited source
evidence and explicitly approve the complete policy before it can control an inspection.
2. Defect-class requirements
2.1. Critical circuit defects
Any open-circuit (OP) or short-circuit (SH) finding is critical and must result in FAIL.
2.2. Conductor scratches
A conductor-scratch (CS) finding requires HUMAN REVIEW before disposition.
2.3. Cosmetic spur allowance
A spur (SP) finding is acceptable for this demonstration and may PASS when no higher-priority rule applies.
2.4. Maximum finding count
More than two actionable PCB defect findings in one image must result in FAIL.
This document is a portfolio example, not a factory acceptance standard. A client must replace these limits
with validated production requirements.

NORTHSTAR ELECTRONICS CONTROLLED QUALITY DOCUMENT
QSP-PCB-017 | Revision 1.0 | Portfolio demonstration Page 2
Confidence and capability controls
Uncertain or unsupported requirements fail safely to human review
3. Detector confidence
3.1. Unconfirmed findings
Findings below 30 percent confidence may be ignored. Findings from 30 percent up to but below 70 percent
confidence require HUMAN REVIEW.
4. Scope boundary
Calibrated length measurements and missing-component checks are outside this example policy. A client deployment must add
camera calibration, a reference assembly, and validated detector capabilities before those requirements can be automated. Any
future requirement that the active detector or rule engine cannot evaluate must produce HUMAN REVIEW rather than an
automatic PASS or FAIL.
Disposition Meaning Required action
PASS No fail or review rule triggered Release under approved process
FAIL One or more fail rules triggered Reject and record decisive evidence
HUMAN REVIEW Uncertain or unsupported requirement Quality engineer resolves disposition
